The adapter accepts input text pairs (x,y) and processes them through the DeBERTa encoder.
The adapter outputs a scalar score $g_{\theta}(x,y)$ representing the energy value for the input pair.
The positive sample terms $-\mathbb{E}_{y^+ \sim p_{data}(y|x)}[g_\theta(x,y^+)] + \alpha\mathbb{E}[g_\theta(x,y^+)^2]$ have been implemented.
The negative sample terms $\mathbb{E}_{y^- \sim p_\theta(y|x)}[g_\theta(x,y^-)] + \alpha\mathbb{E}[g_\theta(x,y^-)^2]$ have been implemented.
The adapter has been trained using the NCE loss and spectral normalization for the specified number of steps.

The NCE loss has been implemented according to Equation (3) in the paper, which includes: $\nabla_{\theta}\ell(\theta) = \nabla_{\theta}\{-\mathbb{E}_{y+\sim p_{data}(y|x)}[g_{\theta}(x,y+)] + \alpha\mathbb{E}[g_{\theta}(x,y+)^2] + \mathbb{E}_{y-\sim p_{\theta}(y|x)}[g_{\theta}(x,y-)] + \alpha\mathbb{E}[g_{\theta}(x,y-)^2]\}$, incorporating both positive and negative sample terms with regularization.
The gradient updates $\nabla_{\theta} \mathcal{L}_{NCE}$ have been implemented with $\eta=5e-6$ as specified in Appendix H.2.
Spectral normalization has been applied to the energy model $g_{\theta}$ to increase gradient stability.
The decomposition of complete solution $y$ into sentence-level sequences $[s_1, s_2, ..., s_L]$ has been implemented.
The autoregressive scoring of sequences using both LLM probabilities and adapter scores has been implemented.
The generation of $M$ samples per beam at each step $l$ based on $p_{LLM}(s_l|x,s_{1:l-1})$ has been implemented.
The scoring of $nk$ candidate chains using the adapter $g_\theta(s_{1:l},x)$ has been implemented.
The selection of top-k beams based on adapter scores has been implemented.
The checking for either reaching $L$ iterations or encountering stop signals has been implemented.
The selection of the highest-scoring complete solution from the $k$ final candidates has been implemented.
The base model generates a set of complete answers in a single step.
The adapter selects the best answer from the candidates as the final response.
The base model generates multiple solution paths using beam search.
The adapter scores and selects the top-$k$ paths at each step, maintaining a beam size of $k=3$ by default as specified in the paper.

Sampling $M$ candidates from adapted inference has been implemented as described in Equation 4 i.e., ${\hat{y}_{i,m}}^M_{m=1} \sim p_{\theta_t}(y|x_i)$
The update of positive samples has been implemented as described in Equation 5 i.e., $y^{(t)}_{i+} = \text{SEL}(y^{(t-1)}_{i+}, {\hat{y}_{i,m}}^M_{m=1})$
The update of negative samples has been implemented as described in Equation 6 i.e., $y^{(t)}_{i-} = {\hat{y}_{i,m} | \hat{y}_{i,m} \neq y^{(t)}_{i+}}^M_{m=1}$
The computation of the loss gradient has been implemented as described in Equation 3 i.e., $\nabla_\theta \ell(\theta_t)$ using $y^{(t)}_{i+}$ and $y^{(t)}_{i-}$
The parameter update has been implemented as described in Equation 7 i.e., $\theta_{t+1} = \theta_t - \eta \nabla_\theta \ell(\theta_t)$
